profiles.name: Dan O'Herlihy
profiles.excerpt: Dan O'Herlihy brought an Irish stage actor's resonant voice into American radio before an Oscar-nominated film career and decades of character work.
profiles.bio_html:
Dan O'Herlihy was born in Wexford, Ireland in 1919 and studied architecture at University College Dublin before acting drew him into the Abbey and Gate theatre worlds. His rich voice quickly proved useful in radio as well as on stage.

After early film work in Britain and Ireland, O'Herlihy moved into an international screen career that included an Academy Award nomination for Robinson Crusoe. Radio remained part of his American career through literary anthology, detective and dramatic programs, where his formal stage training translated especially well to microphone performance.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves ten NBC University Theater performances credited to O'Herlihy, seven Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar appearances, four Lux Radio Theatre broadcasts, three each on The Railroad Hour and The Saint, and additional work on A Man Called X, Let George Do It and Screen Directors Playhouse.

profiles.name: GeGe Pearson
profiles.excerpt: GeGe Pearson was a veteran radio actress whose comedy work on Red Skelton sat alongside a broad West Coast dramatic repertory and later animation voice roles.
profiles.bio_html:
GeGe Pearson was born in 1917 and became a professional radio actress during the medium's network era. She was especially associated with The Red Skelton Show, where she played Sara Dew, but her work extended far beyond one comedy character.

Pearson appeared across suspense, detective and anthology radio while also moving into television and animation. Her later voice work included Crusader Rabbit, showing the continuity between the vocal technique required by radio and the emerging animation business.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves ten The Whistler performances credited to Pearson, six Screen Directors Playhouse appearances, four each on Let George Do It and Wild Bill Hickok, three My Favorite Husband episodes and additional work on Encore Theater, Lux Radio Theatre and The New Adventures of Nero Wolfe.

profiles.name: James Stewart
profiles.excerpt: James Stewart gave radio westerns one of their most distinctive stars as Britt Ponset on The Six Shooter, bringing quiet film naturalism to a medium built entirely on voice.
profiles.bio_html:
James Stewart was born in Indiana, Pennsylvania in 1908 and became one of Hollywood's defining actors after work on Broadway and in film. His screen career included an Academy Award for The Philadelphia Story and a long partnership with directors such as Frank Capra and Alfred Hitchcock.

Radio gave Stewart a major starring vehicle in The Six Shooter, where he played drifting gunfighter Britt Ponset. The role fit Stewart's understated delivery and moral seriousness, creating a western hero whose strength came as much from judgment and empathy as from gunplay. The series lasted only one network season but became one of old-time radio's most admired westerns.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 41 The Six Shooter performances credited to Stewart, making Britt Ponset the clear center of his GRH radio profile.

profiles.name: Joe Forte
profiles.excerpt: Joe Forte was a dependable Hollywood radio character actor whose credits range from westerns and comedy to detective and FBI drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Joe Forte belongs to the supporting repertory that kept Hollywood radio populated with believable minor characters week after week. Personal biography is less extensive than the surviving broadcast record, but his credits show steady professional work across several major genres.

Forte appeared on westerns, detective programs, comedy and anthology drama, moving among productions such as Let George Do It, Wild Bill Hickok, Broadway Is My Beat and This Is Your FBI. That breadth is characteristic of actors valued for flexibility rather than a single signature role.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves six Let George Do It performances credited to Forte, five All Star Western Theatre appearances, four Wild Bill Hickok episodes, three each on Broadway Is My Beat, Lux Radio Theatre, The Great Gildersleeve and This Is Your FBI, plus two Barrie Craig performances.

profiles.name: Norma Varden
profiles.excerpt: Norma Varden moved from concert piano and the British stage into a long Hollywood character career, while radio made frequent use of her polished voice and comic authority.
profiles.bio_html:
Norma Varden was born in London in 1898 and first trained as a concert pianist, studying in Paris and performing professionally in England. She later chose acting, studied at the Guildhall School of Music and Drama, and built a substantial West End career before moving to Hollywood.

Varden became a familiar screen character actress in films ranging from Casablanca to The Sound of Music, but radio was also an important part of her American work. Her cultivated delivery suited literary adaptations, mystery and comedy, and her early professional piano career remains a legitimate second facet of her biography.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 19 NBC University Theater performances credited to Varden, seven Lux Radio Theatre broadcasts, six The Whistler appearances, four The Railroad Hour performances, two Broadway Is My Beat episodes and additional work on Rocky Fortune and Screen Directors Playhouse.

profiles.name: Rosemary Rice
profiles.excerpt: Rosemary Rice began on Broadway as a young performer and grew into a versatile New York radio actress whose career stretched from Archie Andrews to CBS Radio Mystery Theater.
profiles.bio_html:
Rosemary Rice began acting while still young, attended the Professional Children's School in New York and built early stage experience through Broadway plays and musicals. Radio became another major branch of her career, giving her regular work in comedy, serials and drama.

Her best-known continuing radio role was Betty Cooper on Archie Andrews, but Rice also appeared in daytime serials and anthology programs across several decades. She remained active long enough to join both Theater Five in the 1960s and CBS Radio Mystery Theater during the 1970s revival.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 21 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Rice, 16 Theater Five appearances and two Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar performances.

profiles.name: Guy Repp
profiles.excerpt: Guy Repp was a New York radio repertory actor whose surviving credits are especially strong in science fiction, detective drama and wartime anthology work.
profiles.bio_html:
Guy Repp belongs to the professional New York radio repertory whose careers are best reconstructed from the programs themselves. His credits show sustained work across literary drama, wartime productions, crime series and science fiction.

Repp appeared repeatedly on X Minus One and Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar, while programs such as CBS Radio Workshop, The Chase and Words at War used him in changing dramatic roles. That range reflects the central skill of the repertory actor: establishing a complete new character quickly without depending on visual performance.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves nine X Minus One performances credited to Repp, eight Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar appearances, five CBS Radio Workshop broadcasts, three each on The Chase and Words at War, two each on Cloak and Dagger and Columbia Workshop, plus a CBS Radio Mystery Theater appearance.

profiles.name: Lois Corbett
profiles.excerpt: Lois Corbett was a West Coast radio actress whose comedy and dramatic credits place her inside the busy Hollywood repertory of the 1940s and 1950s.
profiles.bio_html:
Lois Corbett was born Lois Virginia Corbet in Des Moines in 1907 and became a professional radio actress before moving into television. She worked in the Hollywood broadcasting community and later married longtime radio announcer Don Wilson.

Her credits crossed feature-film adaptations, comedy and private-eye drama. She appeared repeatedly on Lux Radio Theatre and The Phil Harris-Alice Faye Show, while detective and suspense programs used her for a range of supporting characters.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves ten Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Corbett, nine The Phil Harris-Alice Faye Show appearances, three each on The Adventures of Philip Marlowe and The Halls of Ivy, two each on Escape, Screen Directors Playhouse and The Whistler, plus an A Man Called X appearance.

profiles.name: Robert Easton
profiles.excerpt: Robert Easton began in radio as a teenager and turned an extraordinary ear for dialect into a six-decade acting career and a second profession as Hollywood dialogue coach.
profiles.bio_html:
Robert Easton was born Robert Easton Burke in Milwaukee in 1930 and began performing on radio while still in his teens. He first gained national experience through Quiz Kids, then moved into character acting where his command of regional speech became one of his strongest professional assets.

Easton worked on programs including Fibber McGee and Molly, Gunsmoke, Our Miss Brooks and Suspense. That vocal skill later made him one of Hollywood's leading dialogue and accent coaches, helping other actors master regional and foreign speech while he continued performing himself.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 37 Fibber McGee and Molly performances credited to Easton and one The Halls of Ivy appearance. Those holdings capture the radio foundation of a career later celebrated for its mastery of voices and dialects.

profiles.name: Victor Jory
profiles.excerpt: Victor Jory was a commanding stage and screen actor who also starred in literary radio drama, most notably Dangerously Yours and its successor Matinee Theater.
profiles.bio_html:
Victor Jory was born in 1902 and built a long career in theatre, film and television, often playing forceful or villainous characters. His rich voice and formal delivery also made him a natural radio leading man.

Jory starred in Dangerously Yours beginning in 1944 and continued when the program became Matinee Theater. The series adapted romantic and literary stories for radio, giving Jory a regular starring showcase distinct from his screen image. He also narrated the celebrated 1946 recording of Tubby the Tuba.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 21 Matinee Theater performances credited to Jory, 11 Dangerously Yours broadcasts, two Suspense appearances and additional work on CBS Radio Mystery Theater and CBS Radio Workshop.
